correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(d(x^2+y^2)/(2dt)=y^2z\). Invariance therefore forces zero mean. If the positive and negative weighted parts both vanished, continuity on the invariant support would force \(y^2|z|=0\). Any interval with \(z\ne0\) then forces \(x=y=0\), whence \(\dot z=c\) contradicts compactness for \(c\ne0\). The only remaining possibility \(z\equiv0\) reduces to a harmonic oscillator plus the impossible identity \(x(1+a y)=c\); the checker independently reconstructs the critical algebra. The proof is infinite-time and measure-theoretic, not a finite numerical extrapolation.
